value.a:
Lemelson Vineyards Tikka's Run Pinot Gris 2022 is new on our by-the-glass list from November 2026, our white from Oregon. The glass sheet prints no price, so ask the manager before you quote one.

Lemelson is an estate winery at Carlton, in the Willamette Valley, that has farmed its own vineyards organically from the start. Pinot Gris, PEE-noh GREE, is the grape. Tikka's Run is named for Tikka, the Great Pyrenees who patrolled the edge of the Pinot Gris vines. How the 2022 was fermented and aged is a question for the sommelier.

In the glass it tastes of pear, peach and lemon, and the texture is the point: velvety, soft and full bodied, where the Albariño and the Sauvignon Blanc are lean and crisp.

That weight is why it is the first pick with the Crab & Corn Omelette, where it meets the butter and eggs and its lemon joins the lemon on the plate, and why it is the still white offered with the Turtle Soup.

The label reads Sonoma County, and most of the fruit comes from Alexander Valley, the warm inland valley in the north of the county where Cabernet ripens fully. How long the 2022 spent in oak is a question for the sommelier.

In the glass it tastes of blackberries, cassis and vanilla. It is full bodied, with a velvety texture and soft tannins, so it gives a Cabernet drinker the dark fruit and weight they expect without a hard, drying grip.

It is the second pick with the Roasted Chateaubriand, for the guest who wants Cabernet rather than red Burgundy, and the fuller glass with the Creole-Spiced Hanger Steak. On the list it sits above the Moulin d'Issan and the Durban in weight.

It is the first pick with the Louisiana Crab Claws, where its richness mirrors the brown butter, and the step up from the Gainey with the oysters, the pecan fish, the poussin and the swordfish.

value.a:
Domaine de Courcel Pommard Premier Cru 2007 is our red Burgundy by Coravin, new on the glass list from November 2026 in place of the Inglenook Rubicon. The glass sheet prints no price, so ask the manager before you quote one.

Pommard, poh-MAR, is a village on the Côte de Beaune known for firm, full red Burgundy made from Pinot Noir. Domaine de Courcel, koor-SELL, has been in one family there since the seventeenth century. Its label reads Grand Clos des Épenots, the walled vineyard the domaine owns alone inside the premier cru Les Grands Épenots, which is the name our glass sheet prints.

This bottle is a 2007, almost twenty years old, so the tannins have softened and the fruit is mellow and earthy: dark cherry, plum and spice. The Coravin, a needle through the cork, is how one glass of a wine this old can be poured.

It is the first pick with the Roasted Chateaubriand, and the step up with the Petite Filet Mignon, the Chateau Espagnole and the Lamb Shank en Croûte.
